objective: Estimate the effect of Euclidean versus mesh-edge-shortest-path 8-neighbour graphs in GABI on the existing DoubleDelta benchmark.
fixed: 32,000 field points, values, weights, normals and node ordering
six-layer width-100 latent-100 author GCN, loss and normalization
paired initial weights, per-epoch example order and MMD random draws
batch size 100, 455 epochs, 10,010 updates, AdamW 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, exponential decay to 1e-5
checkpoint with minimum validation reconstruction plus MMD loss
ABC 50,000 normal latent draws, 100 accepted, noise sigma .01, identical saved observation sets
graph_definition: Eight nearest retained vertices by weighted shortest paths on original mesh edges, symmetrised; geometry only.
normalization_note: Only training-set statistics are reused; no trained model parameters are loaded.
primary_metric: Mean hidden-area-weighted nRMSE at 20 saved sensors; paired surface minus euclidean difference.
inference_seed: Training seed is also ABC seed; matched across graph variants.
uncertainty: Report each paired seed. Geometry bootstrap of seed-averaged differences, retaining all nine angles within a physical geometry; conditional on the three trained pairs.
test_gate: All six runs and validation scores complete and finite; paired initialization/order checks pass; development report written and source/checkpoint hashes sealed. Evaluate both variants and all seeds regardless of development ranking.
selection_policy: No graph, seed, hyperparameter or checkpoint selection using test outcomes; no tuning in this ablation.
limitations: CUDA scatter reductions may not be bitwise deterministic.
Mesh-edge shortest paths approximate intrinsic surface distance.
This is a mesh-derived adaptation, not an exact reproduction of an original GABI dataset.
